card.name: Conditional words in dosing instructions
card.fires_on: Small words like "if", "to" after "up", "any", or "necessary" that open a condition or limit in an instruction, often right after "and,". Mostly in dose-adjustment or monitoring directions.

modes.label: "if" after "and,"
modes.description: The word "if" introduces a conditional action such as "if needed" or "if necessary" after a monitoring or management step.
modes.example: Manage hypertension using standard antihypertensive treatment and,<< if>> needed, interrupt, reduce or discontinue

modes.label: Limits and caps
modes.description: Words like "to" after "up" or "maximum" set an upper limit on a delay or number of doses.
modes.example: The dosing period may be extended for dose delays up<< to>> day 10 of the cycle.

modes.label: "necessary" after "If"
modes.description: "necessary" completes a condition that allows a change in schedule.
modes.example: If<< necessary>>, the scheduled injection day may be changed

card.plain: It marks the spot in an instruction where a condition or a limit is about to be stated, such as "if needed" or "up to".
